summary: The supervisor's tip-claim handoff is decoded three times under three disagreeing predicates, so a present-but-unusable value runs a tick with no claim on the ref it moves
acceptance: one decode answers every question this run asks of the handoff — the pid a tick treats as its own claim, whether it acquires one, and whether it is the supervised child whose wave reads the stop flag — and a handoff value that names no pid refuses at the point of detection rather than proceeding under three readings of it
tests: a tick refuses when the supervisor tip-claim handoff carries a value that names no pid
notes: Verified this tick: `src/cli.ts:1031` reads `FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD` by truthiness, `:1041` (cdacc8b1) by `!== undefined`, `:1272` by `=== undefined`. An empty value skips `acquireTipClaim`, sets `ownTipClaimPid` to this process's own pid *and* answers `supervisedRun` true — a bare tick moving the ref unclaimed whose wave then honors the stop flag spec/loop.md promises it ignores. A non-numeric value is `NaN` at `:1032`, never matching `src/tipVerify.ts:44`.
